title: It Snowed in New York in June 1816. A Volcano Did It

scenes.text: In June 1816, it snowed in New York.
A foot of snow in New England. Frost in July. Summer lakes iced over.
A year earlier, Mount Tambora in Indonesia had exploded, blowing 4,000 feet off its own peak.
31 cubic miles of ash went into the sky, wrapped the planet and dimmed the Sun.
Crops failed from America to China. Grain prices quadrupled. The year without a summer.
One volcano. Snow in June, half a world away.

description:
In 1816, snow fell in Albany, New York, and across New England in June, and frost killed crops in July and August. It became known as the Year Without a Summer.
The cause was Mount Tambora in Indonesia, which erupted in April 1815, lost about 4,000 feet of height and hurled roughly 31 cubic miles of ash and gas into the atmosphere, dimming sunlight around the world. Grain prices in the US at least quadrupled.
What would you do if it snowed in the middle of summer? Comment below.
first_comment: Bonus: the gloomy, rained-out summer of 1816 kept Mary Shelley indoors in Switzerland, where she wrote Frankenstein. What is the strangest weather you have ever seen?
